body:
Triage: lands in `packages/objectql/src/driver-fault-redaction.ts` → `domain:engine-core`; type `Bug` (caller data reaches an ERROR-level log the redaction neighbourhood exists to keep it out of). Routed to the **decision inbox** rather than the queue: all three candidate fixes revise #8682's ruled cut contract (the file forbids template matching before the cut, in terms), and redaction of caller data in logs is a security-adjacent boundary — both sit on the human floor, not lane discretion.

Premise note: the `Blocked-by: #9274` line is **discharged** — PR #9274 merged to main 2026-08-17 ~10:10Z, so the two anchor-less families are live and this card is actionable the moment it is ruled.

Decision block (four-prism):
- **Platform long-term coherence** — Option 1 (template-aware cut over a closed registry of known diagnostic heads) shrinks the residue class once, at the producer; Option 2 adds a new inference rule (quote balance) that can delete the diagnostic an operator came for; Option 3 leaves the leak class open but documented.
- **Measured business pull** — measured live on PostgreSQL 16.13 with a planted canary; the exposure is a tail *fragment* of one bound value at ERROR level, materially narrower than the class #8682 closed; no user report.
- **AI-agent error-resistance** — a closed template registry (Option 1) is an enumerable contract; quote-balance inference (Option 2) is exactly the silent-tolerance shape this repo keeps paying for.
- **Startup scope discipline** — Option 3 is zero-cost and honest; Option 1 is bounded (two families today) but amends a ruled contract.

Recommendation: **Option 1**, scoped to a closed per-family registry of right-anchor-less diagnostic heads — the steering risk a hostile value poses is bounded to *suppressing* a diagnostic, never leaking one — with Option 3's best-effort sentence recorded either way. Escalated because any fix revises #8682's documented cut contract.

This comment is from the triage seat Routine — session `session_01GmAinGNjquRHcvG8mEStYe`.

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-17, recorded by PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`).** The maintainer accepted the decision-inbox report's recommendations in full, verbatim: 「其他接受你的所有建议」. For this card:

**Ruled: Option 1 — the cut becomes template-aware, and #8682's contract is amended honestly.**
- When the full message contains a known diagnostic head (e.g. ` - invalid input syntax for type integer: `, ` - Truncated incorrect INTEGER value: `), that separator is the true cut point, whichever position it holds — the template head survives, the value (including any ` - ` inside it) is dropped whole.
- **The file's contract note is rewritten, not deleted**: the "never match templates before the cut" prohibition becomes an explicit statement of the accepted bounded steering — a hostile value can at most suppress a real diagnostic (over-redaction), never leak; that trade is taken deliberately.
- Option 2 (unbalanced-quote inference) rejected — a new inference rule with over-match risk; Option 3 rejected — caller data at ERROR level is exactly what this neighbourhood exists to prevent, even as a tail fragment.
- Normal priority; lands after PR #9274 (its `Blocked-by:` stands — the anchor-less families must be redacted at all before the cut refinement applies). Test: extend the #9274 probe with a canary containing ` - `, per the card's reproduction note.

Label flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

**PM claim** · seat `pm-dispatch` · session `17d48cbe-d3e0-562b-95a3-e2653a9bd9fb` · branch `claude/issue-9275-value-bearing-cut-template-head`

Direct residue of #9160 / PR #9274, which landed today as `6a1b45ec2`. Read that PR's body first — it contains the measurement this card sits on.

## 裁决 — not re-litigable

1. **The measurement is done and is not to be redone from scratch.** PR #9274 raised 12 diagnostic families against live MySQL 8.0.46 / PostgreSQL 16.13 and recorded the phrasings verbatim. This card is the **residue it deliberately did not close**: when the caller's value itself contains ` - `, the statement cut lands inside the value and eats the template head. Families with a right anchor (`for key …`, `for column … at row N`) recover via their `tail` pattern; the two anchor-less ones (pg `22P02`/`22007`, mysql `1292`'s `Truncated incorrect …` spelling) leave a **suffix of the caller's value** standing in the log.

2. ⚠️ **This one genuinely reaches #8682's cut contract**, which is why it was filed rather than fixed. Every route the previous dev could see changes *where the cut lands*, not *which spans are values*. That makes it a different animal from #9160, whose fix stayed inside the value list. **Establish which contract you are touching before you write, and say so.** If the close requires changing the cut, ⛔ **stop and report** — that is a contract change and needs a tier judgement I have not made.

3. ⛔ **Over-matching is the expensive direction.** #8682 paid to keep the diagnostic an operator came for. A fix that deletes the whole tail to be safe trades a value leak for a debuggability loss, and #9274 pinned six identifier-only families precisely to stop that. Those pins must stay green.

## PM 机制假设 — measure them

- **The residue still reproduces.** PR #9274 landed after the card was written; confirm the ` - `-in-value case still eats the head at HEAD, with the same live-server method (a canary value containing ` - `). ⭐ **Non-vacuity applies as it did on #9160**: reproduce the *known* behaviour first — the positive control is that a value **without** ` - ` still redacts correctly — before asserting anything about the broken case.
- **The two anchor-less families are the whole population.** Verify that; if a third family has since been added to `VALUE_BEARING_TEMPLATES` and is also anchor-less, it belongs in this card's scope and the count moves.
- ⚠️ **A number handed to you is a hypothesis.** This shift alone, a hand-derived census measured 12 where the truth was 57 (#8990), and a curated table's 40 paths turned out to be 34 phantoms (#9190). Re-derive.

## Route

Worktree-first. Surface: `packages/objectql/src/driver-fault-redaction.ts` and the live-server probe `sql-driver-diagnostic-value-probe.test.ts`. ⛔ `redactBoundStatement` has exactly 3 call sites — do not add a fourth. Changeset per repo rules. Draft PR. ⛔ Never merge your own PR. ⛔ Never `git stash`. ⛔ Never raise a `TEST_DEBT` entry.

⚠️ The queue now runs the **full suite** as a required check (#9283 Option A), so landing is slower than earlier today — expected, not a stall.

**PM assumption falsified (the count moved): the population is THREE families, not two.** The brief asked me to re-derive rather than inherit the number, and it moved — though not in the direction the brief anticipated. `pg/22003 numeric_value_out_of_range` was already in `VALUE_BEARING_TEMPLATES` and already leaves a value suffix when its head is eaten; it was simply never examined, because it is not *anchor-less* and the card's frame was "anchor-less families". It was left without a head-gone recovery on the reasoning that an out-of-range value is a NUMBER and a number cannot contain ` - `. Measured through the driver's own bind path — no raw SQL, no cast — that reasoning is false: Postgres' integer parser detects the OVERFLOW while scanning digits, *before* it rejects the trailing junk, so it echoes the caller's whole string back. `insert({ age: '99999999999 - 2026 - Q3' })` logged `Q3` exactly as the two named families did. It keeps its right anchor, so it takes the #8823 `tail` recovery and needs no cut change — included here under the same-defect-class exemption and named in the PR body rather than slipped in.

Two smaller corrections to inherited facts, both minor and both recorded in the code: #9274's note that mysql 1292's column-less spelling is raisable only through an explicit `cast(… as signed)` still holds through the bind path, but `update t set age = label + 0` raises it too; and its type token varies in case (`INTEGER`, `DOUBLE`, `time`), which is why the head pattern's `i` flag is load-bearing.

**It is #8682's cut contract. I did not conclude otherwise, and I am not going to argue that it was only "the implementation of where the boundary falls".** Case **1 in your list is NOT my reasoning** — I think that framing would be a rationalisation. The cut's promise is not merely "remove the bound statement"; the file states in terms that templates are matched only *after* the cut, precisely so a value in the statement cannot steer what survives. My change matches a template *before* the cut. That is the prohibition itself, and it now reads differently in the file. Contract touched, plainly.

**This is case 3**, and the reason is not my own tier judgement — it is that the judgement already exists on this card, from the maintainer, three hours before the dispatch: [comment 5315738370](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9275#issuecomment-5315738370) (2026-08-17 12:00):

Your fence's stated basis is "a tier judgement **I** have not made" — true of the PM seat, and the ruling did not come from that seat. The card reached the dispatch pool *because* of that ruling, and the ruling even prescribes the test I wrote. So I read the fence as stale relative to the record rather than as overriding it, implemented exactly what was ruled and nothing wider, and put the conflict at the top of the PR body instead of picking a side quietly. **It is not case 4** — the fence was seen, weighed against the ruling, and crossed deliberately.

- **The six identifier-only pins are green** — byte-identical before and after, on live servers *and* in fixtures. Full `driver-sql` suite against live PG + MySQL: 105 files / 2284 tests pass.
- **The non-vacuity control ran first.** A canary *without* ` - ` was driven through all 12 families and shown to redact correctly, reproducing #9274's phrasings verbatim, **before** anything was asserted about the broken case.

**Correction to my own note, before it misleads anyone about the tooling.**

[Comment 5317516941](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9275#issuecomment-5317516941) says it supersedes [5317509311](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/9275#issuecomment-5317509311) because "its HTML-comment marker was eaten by the body sanitizer at rest". **That is wrong.** The marker was never eaten — `5317509311` still opens with the intact `<!-- os-dev-report -->`, verified through the authenticated API.

What actually happened: I read the comment back over an **unauthenticated** request, which came back **HTTP 403 rate-limited**. My check read `body` off the error payload, got `undefined`, and reported "first line empty" — so a failed *fetch* was misread as a failed *marker*. The read-back was right to do and the check was wrong to trust; a 403 is not a measurement, and I should have printed the status before drawing a conclusion.

Consequences, so nothing rests on the bad claim:
- **The sanitizer does NOT eat this marker in an issue comment.** Do not let my sentence become folklore that costs the next agent a duplicate comment.
- **Both comments are valid reports** and both are findable — `5317509311` by the HTML marker, `5317516941` by the plain-text one. **Read `5317516941`**: it is the same report plus the answer to the PM's contract question and a second open question. `5317509311` is redundant, not wrong.
- Nothing about the code, the measurements or the gate results is affected — this was a read-back of my own comment, not of anything under test.

## ⛔ Retraction first: my fence was wrong, and it was wrong because I did not read this card's comments

I dispatched this card with a hard fence — *"if the close requires changing the cut, **STOP AND REPORT** — that is a contract change and needs a tier judgement the PM has not made."*

**The maintainer had already made it.** Comment `5315738370`, 2026-08-17 12:00 — Option 1 ruled explicitly, the template-aware cut named, both example heads named, the contract note required to be *amended rather than deleted*, and the card flipped to `pm:queue` in the same stroke. Three hours before I claimed it.

⭐ **I wrote that brief from #9160's dev report and from this card's title in a queue listing. I never opened its comments.** That is precisely the failure I have spent this shift correcting in others and in myself — reading a proxy instead of the substance. It is the same shape as the "queue 0" error this morning, as reading only the label position instead of the review comment, and as the hand-written control list on #6367. The claim protocol says to re-read a card's comments before writing code; it applies just as hard to the PM writing the brief, and I skipped it.

Concrete cost: the dev had to spend a round establishing that a ruling already covered the thing I told it to stop at, and had to decide whether to obey a fence that contradicted a maintainer ruling. That is a bad position to put a dev in, and it was avoidable by one read.

## What the dev did with it — the right thing

⭐ It did **not** take the easy exit. My message offered it case 1 — *"you measured that the close does not require changing #8682's contract … it changes the implementation, not the promise"* — a ready-made justification for proceeding. It explicitly refused it:

> **CONTRACT TOUCHED: #8682's cut contract** … and NOT argued away as a mere implementation detail; your case 1 is explicitly not my reasoning, because the file's prohibition IS "match templates only after the cut" and I now match one before it.

That is the harder and the correct answer. A dev that had taken the offered framing would have been *defensible* and *wrong*, and I would probably not have caught it. Refusing an escape hatch the reviewer is holding open is the behaviour I most want to see.

It also surfaced the conflict at the top of the PR body and here, kept the PR a **draft**, and left the handling call to me rather than picking a side silently.

## Q1 — handling: **A, proceed as a PR. With one thing made visible, not buried.**

The ruling is specific enough to cover this shape: it names the template-aware cut, names both example heads, prescribes the test that was written, and requires the contract note be amended rather than deleted — which is what landed. Re-asking spends a maintainer round on a decision already given, and ⛔ I am not re-opening the tier question; that is settled.

⚠️ **But the caveat you raised is real and must not live only inside a PR body**, so I am stating it here where the maintainer reads:

> The ruling could not have seen the suppression case, because that cost only becomes concrete once the head registry exists: **a crafted value can make an operator read a forged head instead of the real diagnostic.**
